A. INSTALLATION OF RED CURB � 1060 WALNUT GROVE AVENUE
SUMMARY
On December 5, 2013, the Traffic Commission reviewed a request from a resident regarding traffic conditions and access to the property at 1060 Walnut Grove Avenue. The resident�s complaints describe a lack of visibility when exiting and entering the property to and from Walnut Grove Avenue and that the lack of visibility creates hazardous conditions. It had been requested that parking restrictions (red curbing) be installed in order to increase visibility for vehicles that are entering and exiting the driveway. At the meeting of December 5, 2013, many nearby residents were opposed to the addition of parking restrictions due to the net loss of one parking space on Walnut Grove Avenue and restrictions to parking on adjacent Landis View Lane. Staff has reviewed the site and determined that by alleviating one stretch of the parking restrictions on Landis View Lane, three parking spots can be gained to offset the one lost due to the installation of red curbing.
Staff Recommendation
It is recommended that the Traffic Commission recommend to the City Council:
1. That approximately 15 feet of red curbing be added to the existing 80 feet of red curbing to the south of the property at 1060 Walnut Grove Avenue; and,
That the posted parking restrictions on the westerly most 90 feet of the north side of Landis View Lane be alleviated and approximately 24 feet of red curbing be installed from the corner of Walnut Grove Avenue, leaving parking for up to 3 vehicles.
4. NEW BUSINESS
A. REVIEW OF TRAFFIC CONDITIONS AT ANGELUS AND KEIM STREET
SUMMARY
A request was received to review traffic conditions at Angelus Avenue and Keim Street. The Principal at Rice Elementary School indicated that there are pedestrian and vehicle safety concerns in this area during school drop-off times, due to the lack of a stop sign and crosswalk at this intersection. A traffic study was conducted at the location, including a warrant study to determine if the installation of stop controls and crosswalks was appropriate. After studying the location, it was determined that the intersection did not meet minimum volume or accident thresholds for the installation of stop controls. However, based on several additional safety factors, the traffic engineer determined that stop controls should be installed in order to increase pedestrian and traffic safety.
Staff Recommendation
That the Traffic Commission:
1. Review the traffic study findings and concur with the traffic engineer�s findings to install stop controls at the intersection of Angelus Avenue and Keim Street; and
2. Recommend the installation of stop controls to the City Council.
